newsitem.title: FINLAND: Handicapped-friendly Helsinki ready for summit.
newsitem.headline: Handicapped-friendly Helsinki ready for summit.

text.p: Handicapped-friendly Finland rolled out the red carpet for wheelchair-bound U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursdy when he arrived for a two-day summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
No changes have had to be made to buildings or different arrangements made for the two-day summit, although a walk in the Helsinki woods with Yeltsin has been dropped.
Clinton's arrival at Helsinki's Vantaa airport was hardly elegant.

Unlike most handicapped plane passengers, who would be wheeled from the plane through the airport terminal, Clinton suffered the indignity of being lowered to the ground in an airport catering truck, probably for security reasons.
A slightly embarrassed Clinton, injured last week in a freak accident, was pushed across a red carpet after being brought down from the aircraft.
Clinton's leg problem is temporary, if serious. Yeltsin, on the other hand, has undergone major heart surgery in the past six months although he now appears to be bouncing back to rude health.
At the Helsinki presidental palace, where Clinton will meet Yeltsin for talks, no special ramps had to be installed.
"Nothing special needed to be done," said Mika Peltonen, head of security at the palace. "We have guests in wheelchairs quite often," he told Reuters.
A planned walkabout for Clinton and Yeltsin in the grounds of the Mantyniemi villa, however, was cancelled.
Clinton, who lost his footing and stumbled down the stairs at the Florida home of Australian golf champion Greg Norman last week, is recovering from surgery to repair a torn knee tendon.
The Inter-Continental Helsinki hotel, where Clinton will stay during the two-day summit, did not have to make changes to suit Clinton's temporary disability.
"Everything is flat and the corridors are wide," said Tom Blomquist, assistant hotel manager. "There are no obstacles to go over."
Doctors said Clinton would use a combination of crutches and a wheelchair during the summit and would need a footstool during his talks with Yeltsin.
Specialists were standing by at Helsinki University Central Hospital for any possible emergencies.
